note: Fern discriminates on a typed one-member enum tag (an inline member need not require it) but not on a bare const (see const-tag-variants-undiscriminated), collapses alike primitive element members, makes a member naming a null-admitting component Optional in its slot, and lends a multi-type list's additionalProperties to its object member; four sub-cases repaired, codosseum already matching since c0d439ecd

array items {type: object, oneOf: [type-less members with properties]} are Fern's named union of Zero/One models (worked as [ItemZero()]), and a model hoisted out of its own recursive base restates that base's fields
a property oneOf of $refs under a discriminator it cannot decide is Fern's named {Owner}{Prop} union alias, not an inline typing.Union
an optional query anyOf [array of inline string enum, null] names its element enum {Op}Request{Param}Item

allOf [open property-less object, oneOf|anyOf of inline objects] is one model of every branch's properties, all optional, each as the first branch declaring it writes it (const and one-member enum tags hoisted as enums), tagged or not

$ref members fixing an unrequired tag with a bare const (no type: string) are a plain typing.Union, each member keeping the tag as a one-value enum; the enum side is union-modelling's singleton-enum-tags

cleared by c0d439ecd5b971e8c1ed81ef107798f1a8659d53 (#672): a component with sibling properties over constraint-only oneOf branches names its variants Zero and the first distinguishing property, as Fern does
ruling 6 inline-union-types: a lone-$ref oneOf element is that reference (its model keeps its tag) and an annotated map beside null is the nullable map, with no named model of crozier's own

ruling 6 inline-union-types: a map value allOf [$ref] is that reference (Optional where it admits null) with no {Name}Value model, and a nested-array map leaf of inline objects is Fern's {Name}ItemItemValue
a 3.0 nullable: true beside a multi-member union is not read onto the alias; only a member naming a null-admitting component is Optional
a one-member union of a type-less patternProperties-only closed object is undocumented Any, and a 3.1 $ref beside oneOf/anyOf is an alias of the reference
a query anyOf of a nullable scalar and an array of it is the named {Op}Request{Param} union with the scalar Optional, not the one-or-many shorthand
a query oneOf of two arrays of one element type is that array read one-or-many: Union[Item, Sequence[Item]]
